title: How Climate Change Affects Animal Migration

blanks.sentence: Animal migration usually happens because of changes in _____.
Wildebeest move through two East African areas depending on the _____.
Migration can also be connected with reproduction, including mating and _____.
Some shark species are able to travel _____.
One example describes great white sharks travelling from Australia to _____.
Climate change affects migration by changing ocean _____.
Sea turtles eat _____, which can absorb carbon.
Managing about ten animal groups could remove around _____ of carbon each year.
Some experts estimate that yearly climate goals require removing _____ of CO2.

multipleChoice.question: How is animal migration introduced in the programme?
options: As movement from one place to another, often linked to weather or temperature
As a rare behaviour found only in ocean animals
As a permanent move caused mainly by human activity
As a journey made only when animals are in danger

multipleChoice.question: Which set of reasons for migration does Trisha give?
options: Avoiding predators, finding shelter and escaping storms
Following human boats, cooling down and resting
Finding food, mating and giving birth
Learning routes, competing and changing colour

multipleChoice.question: What example is used to show that some sharks travel very far?
options: They cross from Kenya to Tanzania each year
Great white sharks have moved from near Perth to South Africa
They swim only around the Maasai Mara
They follow sea turtles along the ocean floor

multipleChoice.question: What effect is climate change having on sharks?
options: It is stopping sharks from eating sea turtles
It is making all sharks stay near Australia
It is increasing the number of sharks immediately
It is altering their migration patterns through ocean-temperature change

multipleChoice.question: Why does the programme mention sea turtles and seagrass?
options: To explain how sharks can indirectly help carbon absorption
To show that sharks mainly eat seagrass
To argue that sea turtles are the main cause of climate change
To prove that ocean plants cannot store carbon

multipleChoice.question: What follows when sharks are present in an area, according to Neil’s summary?
options: Sea turtles protect more seagrass
Less carbon can be absorbed by the seabed
More seagrass remains, so more carbon is absorbed
Climate change immediately stops

multipleChoice.question: What is Sophie’s point about migratory animals?
options: Only sharks matter for climate action
Some migrating species can be an under-recognised climate tool
Migratory animals are too difficult to protect
Climate change has ended most migration

multipleChoice.question: What does Trisha’s research suggest about managing about ten animal groups?
options: It would remove all CO2 from the atmosphere
It would mainly protect tourism
It would produce six gigatonnes of CO2 each year
It could sequester about six gigatonnes of carbon yearly

multipleChoice.question: Why does Sophie add the 10-gigatonne figure?
options: To give scale to the six-gigatonne estimate
To reject Trisha’s research completely
To explain shark migration routes
To show that animal protection is unnecessary

multipleChoice.question: What does the “60%” explanation imply about the six-gigatonne figure?
options: It is a tiny amount that can be ignored
It is exactly equal to the total amount needed
It is a very large share of the estimated yearly removal need
It is unrelated to climate goals
